count_rule: this header's oracle_count must equal the length of oracles[] and the spec §11.2 index total; a mismatch is itself a defect

harness_contract.fields: id, guards, defects, given (literal fixture), when, then, mutation_that_must_fail, operands_source, tolerance, fixture_kind
harness_contract.fixture_kind: literal = every operand value printed in the oracle (buildable without asking a question) · constrained_generator = the fixture is generated at build time from fully stated constraints (values not printable here because they derive from L1/L0 at build time) — the label is explicit per NK-7 so no generator masquerades as literal
harness_contract.n8_rule: an oracle that cannot fail is rejected at review; every oracle here carries a mutation that must fail it
harness_contract.worked_events: the three §11.3 events are development cases — calibrate here, never scored in the evaluation protocol

oracles.given: a built contact ledger + window set
oracles.when: (a) a valence rule changes; (b) an aspect-direction change lands
oracles.then: (a) solver is NOT invoked (invocation counter asserted, not digests alone), windows re-evaluated with new lineage; (b) contacts rebuilt under a new convention_id and dependent windows explicitly invalidated; invalidation follows the geometry-dependency rule
oracles.mutation_that_must_fail: re-solving on (a), or keeping stale windows on (b), fails

oracles.given: a served no-window answer and a served window set
oracles.then: the no-window answer includes its coverage object (searched horizon, relations searched, targets unresolved, unavailable inputs); the window set counts confirmed vs context rows separately
oracles.mutation_that_must_fail: a bare 'no windows', or merged confirmed/context counts, fails

oracles.given: the authority-generation manifest
oracles.when: provenance is read; then a republish under a new label runs with no code change
oracles.then: provenance names ka_gochara; the republish passes from the manifest alone
oracles.mutation_that_must_fail: string-matched branch provenance fails

oracles.given: a class's era, month, and day output rows for one year
oracles.when: provenance of each row is inspected
oracles.then: each row traces to a path operating at that grain (lineage names the grain-operating path); day rows trace only to P6; a month row that is a clipped era curve (identical boundaries and monotone-inherited score) is flagged
oracles.mutation_that_must_fail: clipped-curve month/day rows (the 27-of-41 plateau shape) fail

oracles.given: a P6 day evaluation with a pinned janma-nakṣatra and day nakṣatra (nine-fold count stated; twins case: natal star index 24, transit index 20, zero-based inclusive cyclic distance 24 → nine-fold class 6)
oracles.then: the tārā term is PRESENT with the correct normalised key and class (6 in the fixture); a null key (the case-mismatch defect) or absent term fails; P6 being testimony, the term annotates and does not weight
oracles.mutation_that_must_fail: tārā None (key mismatch) or a wrong nine-fold class fails

oracles.given: producer fixture containing two eligible peaks 60 days apart (< 90), plus the serve layer
oracles.when: producer output vs served output are compared
oracles.then: BOTH peaks survive in the producer output (no producer-side MIN_PEAK_SEPARATION_DAYS filter); the 90-day filter, where applied, exists only at serve time; (v1.0's fixture could reject a correct producer — replaced)
oracles.mutation_that_must_fail: a producer-side 90-day suppression drops one peak and fails

oracles.given: the natal-epoch class birth_anchor, plus a non-empty control class with known rows
oracles.then: ZERO rows for birth_anchor at era/month/day resolutions; the control class returns its known rows (an empty or no-op build fails the control, not just the assertion)
oracles.mutation_that_must_fail: any birth_anchor row, or an empty control, fails

oracles.given: actual mūrti rows in the build
oracles.then: no mūrti row carries verse_cited by computation alone; operator_role = testimony; a window scored WITH vs WITHOUT the mūrti rows is bit-identical (zero scoring effect asserted, not just row provenance)
oracles.mutation_that_must_fail: any scoring delta from mūrti rows fails

oracles.given: BPHS1:16496-16502: ordinary aspects graduated ¼/½/¾/full at 3-10/5-9/4-8/7; specials full; permitted bodies enumerated = the seven grahas (nodes explicitly excluded from dṛṣṭi, N-14)
oracles.then: ordinary aspects carry the graduated fractions; the 7th is full for every graha; Mars 4/8, Jupiter 5/9, Saturn 3/10 full (directed per O-AD); NO nodal aspect rows exist; directed numeric roots asserted via O-AD-1…4
oracles.mutation_that_must_fail: a fractional special, a graduated 7th, or a node-cast aspect row fails
